sources.title: Mikhail Khovanov and Lev Rozansky, Matrix factorizations and link homology II, arXiv:math/0505056v2 (31 Jan 2006), 37 printed pages; published as Geom. Topol. 12 (2008) 1387-1425
sources.locator: Complete 37-page article, sections 1-7: section 1 printed pp. 1-10 (definitions (1)-(6), Figure 6, Propositions 1-2, Markov moves, Theorems 1-2, formula (7), F-definition and unknot normalization); section 2 printed pp. 12-17 (subsection 'Product factorizations, graph homology and Koszul complexes', Proposition 3; subsection 'Maps chi_0, chi_1 revisited', Lemmas 1-2, formulas (8)-(9)); section 3 printed pp. 17-19 (markings, Lemma 3, formula (10)); section 4 printed pp. 20-21 (Propositions 4-5); section 5 printed pp. 21-24 (Proposition 6); section 6 printed pp. 24-35 (Proposition 7, Figure 20, Proposition 8, Lemmas 4-9); section 7 printed pp. 35-36 (Euler characteristic relations and proof of Theorem 2)

read_evidence.method: Full 37-page PDF (303442 bytes, sha256_16 1b6580406c3d35b5) downloaded from arXiv, text extracted with MuPDF, and every numbered display, proposition, lemma, theorem, figure caption and the complete proof sections 2-7 read in the extracted text; the LaTeX source of the paper (arXiv e-print) was additionally downloaded and inspected to resolve the Figure 6 / negative-crossing display conflict (source file hom1.tex lines 217-262 and the cones.eps figure labels).

contents.name: Section 1 opening: R=Q[a,x_i], bigrading (1) deg a=(2,0), deg x_i=(0,2), factorization M=(M^0,M^1,d) with d of bidegree (1,1) and d^2=w, morphisms, homotopies of bidegree (-1,-1), hmf_w
Figure 3 lattice visualization and the remark that an empty index set makes mf_w the category of 2-periodic complexes over Q[a]
formula (2): the arc factorization R -> R{-1,1} -> R with potential a(x_1-x_2)
formulas (3)-(4): the wide-edge tensor factorization with potential a(x_1+x_2-x_3-x_4)
C(Gamma) for a planar marked graph, internal versus boundary variables, infinite rank, Figure 4 example
closed graphs: w=0, 2-periodic complex, contractible summands 0->Q[a]->Q[a]->0, termwise cohomology H(Gamma)
the single circle with one mark: Q[a,x] -> Q[a,x]{-1,1} -> 0 and H(Gamma) = Q[x]{-1,1}
presentation matrices P_0,P_1 for C(Gamma_0) and Q_0,Q_1 for C(Gamma_1) with the displayed term shifts
formula (5): chi_0 given by U^0_0,U^1_0, homogeneous of bidegree (0,2)
formula (6): chi_1 given by U^0_1,U^1_1, bidegree-preserving
Figure 6: the two crossing complexes with their shifts {0,2} and {0,-2} and the maps chi_0 and chi_1
positive crossing complex 0 -> C(Gamma_0){0,2} --chi_0--> C(Gamma_1) -> 0 with C(Gamma_1) in degree 0

negative crossing complex: the prose repeats the chi_0 display, but Figure 6, (6), the degree typing, the IIa proof and the published formula (13) force 0 -> C(Gamma_1){0,-2} --chi_1--> C(Gamma_0){0,-2} -> 0
C(D) = tensor product of crossing complexes and arc factors, its differential partial, and the category K(hmf_w)
termwise cohomology CH^j(D), trivial a-action, trigraded H(D) = sum H^j_{k,l}(D) and Euler characteristic <D>
Proposition 1: C(D) does not depend on the number of markings
braid diagrams, the restriction to clockwise braids, the Markov move list (a),(b),(c), and the statement that IIb is avoided and not proved
Reidemeister moves I, IIa, IIb, III; only the type III move with coherent orientations and the IIa move are used
Proposition 2: invariance of C(D) under R1, IIa and III up to an overall shift in the triple grading
Theorem 1: H(D1) and H(D2) are isomorphic up to an overall trigrading shift for two braid diagrams of one oriented link
the five defining properties of the function F (conjugation, braid moves, the two stabilization rules, the skein relation, the unknot value) and alpha=-t^{-1}q^{-1}
the normalized series and formula (7), q sqrt(alpha) F(D sigma^{-1}) - (q sqrt(alpha))^{-1} F(D sigma) = (q-q^{-1}) F(D), with unknot value alpha/(1-q^{-2})
Theorem 2: the Euler characteristic <D> of H(D) equals F(D), including finiteness of the trigraded pieces
remark: the reduced theory obtained by passing to the difference ring and the splitting H(D) = reduced tensor Q[x]
contents.reason: The reduced/unreduced comparison and the extra polynomial factor are the topic of the Hochschild comparison pair (order 765); this pair keeps the unreduced matrix-factorization theory only, so the reduced refinement is deliberately not built here.

contents.name: remarks: the n=0/Alexander specialization, the Gornik/Lee deformations, and the prospect of U(n)-equivariant potentials x^{n+1}+a_n x^n+...+a_1 x
contents.reason: Deformation and equivariant upgrades of the potential are not part of the commissioned pair, whose object is exactly the a-sum potential and its HOMFLYPT Euler characteristic.

contents.name: remarks: comparison with the triply graded theories of Asaeda-Przytycki-Sikora and Audoux-Fiedler for braid-like isotopies
contents.reason: Those theories are different invariants of links in I-bundles and of braid-like isotopies; the comparison is not needed for any claim of this pair and no library page owns it.

contents.name: illness remarks: failure on cobordisms and the absence of a Frobenius structure over the empty link
contents.reason: Functoriality and cobordism/TQFT structure are deliberately outside this pair's scope (the sources do not build it and no consumer on this page uses it).

contents.name: section 2.1: the elementary row transformation [ij]_lambda and its inverse
section 2.1, Proposition 3: exclusion of an internal variable occurring in a row (0, y-mu) is a chain homotopy equivalence
section 2.1: the Koszul standard form of graph factorizations, the collapse of the grading, and the triviality of the a-action on closed-graph cohomology
section 2.2: the flip morphisms psi(y), psi'(y) and Lemma 1 (their compatibility with row operations)
section 2.2, Lemma 2: chi_0 = Id (x) psi'(x_4-x_2) and chi_1 = Id (x) psi(x_4-x_2) under the Koszul forms (8), (9)
section 3, Lemma 3 and Figure 10: removing a mark is a local isomorphism of factorizations
section 3, formula (10) and Figure 11: compatibility of mark removal with the two-term chi_1 complexes
section 4, Proposition 4: the type IA kink gives C(D_1) = C(D_2){1,1}[1]
section 4, Proposition 5: the type IB kink gives C(D_1) = C(D_2) with no shift
section 5, Proposition 6 and Figures 15-16: invariance under the braid-like Reidemeister IIa move
section 6, Proposition 7: the decompositions C(Gamma_1)=C(Gamma_4){0,2} + Upsilon and C(Gamma_3)=C(Gamma_2){0,2} + Upsilon
section 6, Proposition 8 and Figures 17-20: invariance under the braid-like Reidemeister III move
section 6, Lemmas 4-9: indecomposability of the reduced complex, nonvanishing bidegree-zero hom spaces, and nonvanishing of the coefficients lambda_b
section 7: the cone relations <D sigma_i> = <D e_i> - q^2<D> and <D sigma_i^{-1}> = q^{-2}(<D e_i> - <D>), their elimination to the skein relation, and the proof of Theorem 2
section 7: the unknot Euler characteristic t^{-1}/(q^{-1}-q) and the normalization of F
section 7 closing remark: the construction works over any field and over Z
contents.reason: This pair fixes the coefficient field Q as in the source's main construction; the integral refinement is not needed by any item and raises separate homological-finiteness questions.

read_evidence.method: Full 40-page published PDF (6-page chunks as served by MSP; mutool reports 40 pages) downloaded from the publisher, text extracted with MuPDF, formulas (12)-(13), the degree assignments and Figure 6 inspected; the extraction of formula (13) shows chi_1 : C(Gamma_1)^{-1/2} -> C(Gamma_0)^{1/2} explicitly.
read_evidence.scope: abstract and section 1, formulas (12)-(13), printed pp. 1387 and 1393-1394

contents.name: abstract: a complex of bigraded vector spaces is assigned to a braid closure and its Euler characteristic is the HOMFLYPT polynomial
formula (12): positive crossing complex with C(Gamma_0) in degree -1/2, C(Gamma_1) in degree 1/2 and differential chi_0
formula (13): negative crossing complex with C(Gamma_1) in degree -1/2, C(Gamma_0) in degree 1/2 and differential chi_1
Figure 6 of the published version: the two crossing complexes with the named maps

sources.title: Mikhail Khovanov and Lev Rozansky, Matrix factorizations and link homology, arXiv:math/0401268v2 (2004); published as Fund. Math. 199 (2008) 1-91
sources.locator: Introduction, printed pp. 2-12: the (R,w)-duplex and matrix-factorization definitions, the cyclic Koszul complex, C(Gamma) for planar graphs, the arc factorizations L_i^j and wide-edge factorizations C_t, the maps chi_0, chi_1 of Figure 8, the positive and negative crossing complexes of Figure 9, the Reidemeister-invariance statement and the Euler characteristic P_n(L)

read_evidence.method: Full 109-page PDF (776289 bytes) downloaded from arXiv, text extracted with MuPDF, and the introduction read in full, including the definitions of (R,w)-factorizations, the graph factorization C(Gamma), the crossing complexes with chi_0 and chi_1, the invariance statement and the Euler characteristic; used as an independent parallel treatment of the same matrix-factorization machinery for the sl(n) specialization.

contents.name: Definitions 1-2 and the homotopy category HMF: (R,w)-duplex, matrix factorization M^0 -> M^1 -> M^0 with d^2=w, homomorphisms and homotopies
C(Gamma) for a plane resolution: arcs L_i^j, wide edges C_t, markings and boundary points, C(Gamma) = tensor of the local factorizations
Figure 8 and the maps chi_0, chi_1 between C(Gamma_0) and C(Gamma_1)
Figure 9 and the crossing complexes 0 -> C(Gamma_0) --chi_0--> C(Gamma_1) -> 0 for a positive crossing and 0 -> C(Gamma_1) --chi_1--> C(Gamma_0) -> 0 for a negative crossing
the invariance statement that diagrams related by a Reidemeister move give isomorphic complexes in the appropriate homotopy category (Theorem 2 stated in the introduction)
the Euler characteristic P_n(L) = sum (-1)^i q^j dim H^{i,j}_n(L) and the n=0,1,2,3 specializations
comparison of the n=2 theory with Khovanov homology and of the n=3 theory with a foam theory
contents.reason: The sl(2)/sl(3) specializations and their foam models belong to the Khovanov-homology literature, not to this pair's matrix-factorization construction for HOMFLYPT; no item here uses them.

contents.name: tangle-cobordism functoriality and the 2-dimensional TQFT sections (sections 9-10 of the paper)
contents.reason: Functoriality and TQFT structure are explicitly outside this pair's commissioned scope; the page stops at the link-level trigraded invariant.

sources.title: Tina Kanstrup (notes by Corina Keller and Wai-kit Yeung), Knot homologies and matrix factorizations, ICMS summer school 'Geometric representation theory and low-dimensional topology' (June 2019), lecture notes
sources.locator: Lectures 1-2 in full (printed pp. 1-7) and the opening of Lecture 3 (printed p. 8): link homologies, Markov's theorem, the HOMFLYPT skein normalization, the triply graded invariant via Soergel bimodules and via matrix factorizations

read_evidence.method: Full 11-page PDF (336087 bytes) downloaded from the Edinburgh page hosting the notes, text extracted with MuPDF, and the complete notes read; used as an independent lecture-note exposition for the definition of matrix factorizations, the statement of the triply graded invariant, Markov's theorem, and the relation to the Rouquier/Soergel and Hochschild constructions.

contents.name: Definition 1.1: links as collections of knots
Definition 1.2 and Example 1.1: the HOMFLYPT polynomial in the (a,q) skein normalization and a sample computation
contents.reason: The normalization and skein relation of the HOMFLYPT polynomial used in this run are owned by the in-run Hecke-Markov page (def-homflypt-polynomial-from-the-hecke-markov-trace, thm-the-homflypt-skein-relation); the notes' different (a,q) normalization is not adopted.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1 (Markov): links up to isotopy correspond to braids up to Markov moves
Definition 1.3, Theorem 1.2 (Soergel), Theorem 1.3 (Rouquier) and Example 1.2: Soergel bimodules and Rouquier complexes categorifying the Hecke algebra
contents.reason: The Soergel-bimodule and Rouquier-complex categorification is the subject of the in-run pair rouquier-complexes-and-categorical-braid-relations (order 761), which owns these results for this run.

contents.name: Definition 1.4 and Theorem 1.4 (Khovanov): the triply graded Hochschild/Soergel construction of HHH and its invariance up to grading shift under Markov moves
contents.reason: The Hochschild homology route to the triply graded invariant is the subject of the in-run pair hochschild-homology-and-triply-graded-link-homology (order 765), which owns the HHH definition and its invariance.

contents.name: Conjecture 1.1 (Gorsky-Negut-Rasmussen) and Theorem 1.5 (Oblomkov-Rozansky): the Hilbert-scheme and matrix-factorization models of the invariant
contents.reason: The Hilbert-scheme and BPS-sheaf models of HHH are far beyond this pair's scope and belong to ongoing research; no item of this page depends on them.

contents.name: Definition 2.1, Remark 2.1 and Theorem 2.1 (Orlov): matrix factorizations on an affine scheme, their homotopy category and triangulated structure
Remark 2.2, Definition 2.2, Remark 2.3 and the functoriality discussion: strongly and weakly equivariant matrix factorizations, Chevalley-Eilenberg corrections, tensor and pushforward functors
contents.reason: Equivariant matrix factorizations and their functoriality are not used by the KR II construction treated here; this pair works with the bigraded free polynomial-ring model only.

contents.name: Section 2.2 and Proposition 2.1: convolution products, Knorrer reduction, the affine braid group action on matrix factorizations and the n=2 example
contents.reason: The convolution/quiver model of braid actions is a different construction (the Oblomkov-Rozansky route) and is not needed for the Khovanov-Rozansky crossing-complex construction of this pair.

contents.name: Section 2.3 and Theorem 2.2 (Oblomkov-Rozansky): the Hilbert-scheme formulation of the doubly graded invariant
contents.reason: The Oblomkov-Rozansky Hilbert-scheme invariant is a distinct construction whose comparison to KR homology is not established on this page; it is not used by any item.

contents.name: Lecture 3: Conjecture 3.1 (GNR), Definitions 3.1-3.2 (dg-modules), Theorem 3.1 (Arkhipov-Kanstrup), Theorem 3.2 (Bezrukavnikov-Yun), Theorem 3.4 (Ben-Zvi-Francis-Nadler), Theorem 3.5 (Ben-Zvi-Nadler) and the loop-space examples
contents.reason: Derived algebraic geometry, dg-schemes and the GNR conjecture are outside the library's commissioned scope for this pair and are not prerequisites of any item here.
